links.comparator_used: No post-processing (NPP) of the ML-predicted dose, combined with either RayStation mimicking (RSM) or isodose-based mimicking (IBM)
links.outcome: Robustness of IMPT plans in worst-case scenarios, and OAR sparing, compared with manual plans
links.effect: Overly optimistic post-processing compromised plan robustness. Even with RSM partially compensating, 65% of patients in the PP plans did not achieve the expected robustness levels. NPP-RSM gave the best trade-off between robustness and OAR sparing.
links.tradeoff: Post-processing lowered the predicted dose to organs, which meant more OAR sparing on paper but less robust, less deliverable plans.
links.quote: However, too optimistic post-processing applied to the dose prediction (i.e. important decrease of the dose to the organs) compromised the robustness of the plans.

design_hint: pre-deployment robustness evaluation and tuning of post-processing and dose-mimicking parameters
